headline: Daily market snapshot – 30 October 2026
summary: Pre-market on Friday 30 October 2026: S&P 500 futures -0.89%, Nasdaq-100 futures -1.85%, driven by Amazon and Intel post-earnings weakness. Brent crude ~$116 on Hormuz/Houthi attacks. Gold below $4,000 at ~$3,987 on hot PCE and Fed hold. BTC ~$78,200 on Binance $6.3B hack. Oct 29 closes: S&P 500 at 7,720.39 (-0.3%), Nasdaq at 26,184.72 (-1.38%).

headline: Amazon Q3 2026 EPS misses estimates despite AWS strength; capex surges to $77B
summary: Amazon reported Q3 2026 revenue of $201.9B (+12% YoY), missing the $202.3B consensus, and EPS of $1.89 vs the $1.96 estimate. AWS was a bright spot at $46B revenue (+39%), beating expectations. Operating income of $28.1B (+61% YoY) beat forecasts, but capex of $77.3B—far above the $57.5B estimate—and weak Q4 guidance ($240-247B) sent shares down 5-8% after hours.

headline: Amazon AWS +39% to $46B, ad revenue $19.6B; huge capex hike triggers sell-off
summary: Amazon's AWS cloud unit grew 39% to $46B in Q3 2026, beating the $45.3B consensus, while advertising revenue reached $19.64B. However, total capital expenditures came in at $77.3B for the quarter—well above analyst expectations of $57.5B—reflecting aggressive AI infrastructure investment. The steep capex overshoot and below-consensus Q4 guidance drove a sharp after-hours drop.

headline: Microsoft Q1 FY2027 revenue $92.3B beats; Azure +48%, cloud RPO surges 73%
summary: Microsoft reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $92.3B (+19%), beating the $90.58B estimate, with GAAP EPS of $4.92 (up 32%). Azure cloud revenue grew 48%, and Microsoft Cloud total revenue hit $63.9B (+30%). Commercial remaining performance obligations surged 73% to $677B, signaling strong forward demand. Shares rose ~4%.

headline: Intel Q3 2026 beats EPS but Q4 guide disappoints; shares fall pre-market
summary: Intel posted Q3 2026 revenue of $16.5B (+21% YoY), beating the $16.44B estimate, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52, above the $0.41 consensus. However, Q4 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $15-16B and non-GAAP EPS of just $0.25, well below expectations, sending shares lower in pre-market trading. CEO Lip-Bu Tan cited near-term PC industry headwinds.
key_facts: Strongest data center revenue growth in 15 years

headline: Alphabet Q3 2026: first top-and-bottom miss in 4 years; FCF goes negative; stock sinks 10%+
summary: Alphabet reported Q3 2026 revenue of $127.6B (+25% YoY), with adjusted EPS of $2.67 missing the $3.02 consensus—its first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years. Free cash flow turned negative at -$9.07B as capex hit $51.36B. CFO Ashkenazi said 2027 capex will increase significantly, spooking investors and driving shares down more than 10% after hours and 12.6% in the subsequent session.
key_facts: Stock -10%+ AH, then -12.6% in following session

headline: Bernstein cuts Alphabet to Market Perform, lowers price target from $385 to $325 on FCF miss
summary: Bernstein downgraded Alphabet following the company's Q3 2026 earnings miss, lowering its price target from $385 to $325 and moving to a Market Perform rating. The bank cited negative free cash flow and escalating capital expenditure as key concerns weighing on the stock's investment case.
key_facts: Bernstein downgraded GOOGL to Market Perform
Negative FCF and capex escalation cited as concerns

headline: Fed holds at 3.75-4.00% in split 10-2 vote; Dec hike odds rise to ~75-85%
summary: The Federal Reserve held the federal funds target range at 3.75-4.00% on October 28, 2026, in a 10-2 vote with Governors Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike. Chair Warsh said the Fed was waiting for more information before acting, noting politics played 'no role' ahead of midterm elections. Markets now price a 73-85% probability of a December rate hike.
key_facts: Fewer rate meetings planned from 2027 (7 of 8)

headline: ECB holds rates at 2.50%; Lagarde announces February departure; Dec hike 67% priced
summary: The European Central Bank held all three key rates steady on October 29, 2026, keeping the deposit rate at 2.50%, as euro-area inflation hit 3.8%—its highest since September 2023—driven by energy prices. Markets priced a 67% chance of a December hike. President Lagarde confirmed she will depart in February, adding uncertainty to the ECB's policy outlook.
key_facts: Energy prices driving upside inflation risk
Governing Council discussed hike but voted unanimously to hold

headline: Brent crude surges to ~$116 as Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites escalate; 4th monthly gain
summary: Brent crude traded near $116 per barrel on October 30, 2026, driven by escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities and continued Hormuz tanker incidents. WTI rose to ~$103. Both benchmarks were on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain in October, with WTI up roughly 14%. The December Brent contract expires today, with January Brent trading about $4 lower.
key_facts: Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites

headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities push Brent above $116, WTI past $103
summary: New Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites and a tanker incident in the Strait of Hormuz drove Brent crude above $116 and WTI past $103 on Friday. Regional crude exports have managed to partially rebound but remain vulnerable to the escalating US-Iran conflict, which has persisted for months and kept oil on a sustained upward trajectory.

headline: Binance suffers $6.3B breach—largest crypto hack in history; North Korea suspected
summary: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, confirmed a $6.3 billion security breach on October 29-30, 2026, the largest crypto theft ever recorded. Nearly $3 billion has been frozen on-chain. Initial investigation points to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop enabling unauthorized withdrawals. Chainalysis and TRM Labs attributed the attack to North Korea. Binance paused withdrawals but said deposits were unaffected and promised to cover all losses.
key_facts: $6.3B stolen from Binance—largest crypto hack in history
Binance co-founder Yi He: exchange will cover all losses
Withdrawals expected to resume within 48 hours

headline: Bitcoin drops to $76,443 as Binance $6.3B hack triggers $1.57B in crypto liquidations
summary: Bitcoin fell to a session low of $76,443 on October 30 after news of a $6.3B Binance security breach triggered $1.57B in crypto liquidations across the market. BNB fell significantly harder than Bitcoin, which lost about 2% while recovering from lows. The Fear and Greed Index dropped from 51 to 30. October is on track to close down ~6.5% from the month's opening level of ~$83,600.

headline: Gold slips below $4,000 to ~$3,987 as hot PCE data reinforces December Fed hike case
summary: Gold fell below $4,000 to approximately $3,987 per troy ounce on October 30, 2026, marking a second consecutive monthly loss. Hot September PCE inflation data (+3.6% YoY, highest since late 2025) and the Fed's hold with hawkish dissents strengthen the case for a December rate hike, pressuring non-yielding gold. Silver also dropped sharply (~3%).
key_facts: September PCE 3.6% YoY backs December hike
~75% market probability of December Fed hike

headline: US Q3 2026 GDP +3.4% annualized, beats 3.0% forecast; consumer spending flat
summary: The US economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in Q3 2026, beating the consensus estimate of around 3.0-3.1% and accelerating from 2.2% in Q2. However, real consumer spending was flat month-over-month in September, and inflation-adjusted after-tax income fell 0.3%. The strong growth print alongside sticky inflation offers the Fed a mixed picture ahead of potential December rate action.
key_facts: Real consumer spending flat month-over-month in Sep
Strong GDP + sticky inflation complicates Fed path

headline: US September PCE inflation rises to 3.6% YoY; core PCE +3.1%; energy shock persists
summary: US headline PCE inflation rose to 3.6% year-over-year in September 2026, up from 3.4% in August, driven by war-related energy price increases. The monthly PCE gain was 0.5%, its largest in months. Core PCE (ex-food and energy) was +3.1% YoY and +0.3% monthly, the most in four months. The hot print raises the likelihood of a December Fed rate hike.
key_facts: Cleveland Fed Q4 core PCE nowcast ~3.3% annualized
December Fed hike odds ~75-85% following release

headline: Anthropic files S-1 for Nasdaq IPO targeting $1.5-2T valuation; $518B in commitments; $80.7B net loss
summary: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on October 26, 2026 for a planned Nasdaq IPO under ticker ANT, targeting a valuation of $1.5-2 trillion. The filing reveals $16.3B in H1 2026 revenue but an $80.7B net loss, reflecting enormous AI infrastructure costs and $518B in future computing commitments. The company's last private valuation was $965B (May 2026). The IPO is expected in November 2026.

headline: Tesla, SpaceX form independent special committees to explore merger; no terms yet
summary: Tesla and SpaceX have each formed independent board committees to evaluate a potential merger, after Elon Musk confirmed the companies are exploring a combination. No terms, exchange ratio, or timeline have been agreed. Shareholder approval would require 50% of all Tesla shares. Tesla shares closed above $400 on October 27 for the first time since July, driven by merger optimism. Polymarket odds for an official announcement by end-2026 stand at 12.5%.
key_facts: Both companies formed independent special merger committees
No terms, exchange ratio, or timeline agreed
Musk is conflicted party; cannot participate in committee discussions
Shareholder approval needs >50% of all TSLA shares
Polymarket: 12.5% chance by end-2026, 65% by end-2027

headline: US equity futures slide Friday on Amazon, Intel earnings misses; Nasdaq-100 futures -1.85%
summary: US equity index futures fell in early Friday trading on October 30, 2026, as Amazon and Intel shares slid after disappointing Q3 earnings. S&P 500 futures fell 0.89% and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 1.85%. Dow futures were roughly flat. Thursday's session saw the Nasdaq Composite down 1.38% to 26,184 and the S&P 500 off 0.3% to 7,720 on Alphabet's earnings-driven selloff.
key_facts: AMZN and INTC slide driving futures weakness
Alphabet -12.6% on Oct 29 from Q3 miss

headline: Nikkei 225 falls ~2% in volatile Friday session on AMZN/INTC earnings fears
summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell approximately 2.06% in Friday's session, weighed by pre-market weakness in US technology stocks following Amazon and Intel's disappointing Q3 results. The index was near 63,326, pulling back from the prior session's partial recovery.
key_facts: AMZN/INTC earnings miss spilled over to Asia tech

headline: London FTSE 100 edges higher Friday as ECB hold and Shell rally offset tech weakness
summary: London's FTSE 100 gained approximately 0.3%, benefiting from a Shell-driven rally and investor relief following the ECB's October 29 rate hold, even as US tech futures remained weak. The FTSE 100 was near 10,748. The Bank of England's next rate decision is scheduled for November 5.
key_facts: ECB hold on Oct 29 reassured investors

headline: DAX rises 1.31% on ECB hold to near 26,040 despite inflation at 3.8%
summary: Germany's DAX gained 1.31% on October 29, closing near 26,040, as the ECB's decision to hold rates steady at 2.50% provided relief to European equities despite euro-area inflation rising to 3.8%. Markets interpreted the hold as a policy pause before a potential December hike.

headline: Wells Fargo upgrades eBay; sees Depop and live commerce offsetting workforce cost cuts
summary: Wells Fargo upgraded eBay, citing diminished downside earnings risks as workforce reductions are expected to subsidize the company's investments in Depop and live commerce. The bank sees the valuation as attractive following recent underperformance.
key_facts: Workforce reductions to fund Depop/live commerce

headline: Deutsche Bank upgrades PDD Holdings to Buy with $105 target: 'too attractive to look past'
summary: Deutsche Bank upgraded PDD Holdings to Buy with a $105 price target, citing a valuation it described as 'too attractive to look past.' The upgrade reflects confidence that Temu and Pinduoduo's operating leverage outweigh macro uncertainty in China e-commerce.
key_facts: Deutsche Bank upgraded PDD to Buy

headline: Mizuho upgrades Hilton to Outperform, raises target to $421
summary: Mizuho upgraded Hilton Worldwide to Outperform from Neutral and set a new $421 price target, reflecting confidence in the hospitality group's revenue per available room trajectory and brand expansion strategy heading into 2027.
key_facts: Mizuho upgraded HLT to Outperform (from Neutral)

headline: Argus upgrades Biogen to Buy citing Rare Diseases portfolio strength
summary: Argus Research upgraded Biogen to Buy, pointing to the strength of the company's Rare Diseases portfolio as a key driver for earnings growth. The upgrade reverses prior caution following recent pipeline progress.

headline: Argus downgrades Wendy's to Sell on $7.35/share buyout proposal
summary: Argus Research downgraded Wendy's to Sell following a buyout proposal valuing shares at $7.35 each in cash, citing concerns that the offer may not be consummated at that price and limited upside from current levels.

headline: Analyst actions: Meta and Generac upgraded; Netflix and Intuit downgraded on valuation/growth
summary: Multiple analyst rating changes on Friday: Meta Platforms and Generac were upgraded, while Netflix and Intuit were downgraded on valuation and growth concerns. Meta's upgrade follows its recent strong earnings, while Netflix's downgrade reflects concerns about subscriber deceleration and valuation after a recent run-up.

headline: US midterm elections November 3 loom; historical pattern points to post-vote market rally
summary: US midterm elections are scheduled for November 3, 2026, and are drawing investor attention given their potential impact on fiscal policy and congressional balance of power. Historical patterns show midterm election years tend to be weak for stocks, but the 12 months following midterms have produced average gains of 12.4%. The Fed held rates ahead of the vote, with Warsh explicitly noting politics played 'no role.'
key_facts: Fed held pre-election (Warsh: 'politics played no role')

headline: Coinbase Q3 2026 revenue ~$1.22B (flat); adjusted EBITDA +60%
summary: Coinbase reported Q3 2026 net revenue plus other revenue totaling approximately $1.22B, roughly in line with the $1.21B consensus but down significantly from $1.87B in Q3 2025. Adjusted EBITDA improved 60% year-over-year, helped by cost discipline. Block also reported strong results. Both stocks jumped ~12% following the releases, breaking a four-quarter miss streak for Coinbase.
key_facts: COIN and Block (XYZ) each up ~12% post-earnings

summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron both release Q3 2026 earnings on October 30. Goldman Sachs estimated Exxon's Q3 EPS at ~$4.10, above the FactSet consensus of $3.87, driven by a $4.5B refining windfall and 39% jump in upstream earnings. Chevron's consensus calls for EPS of ~$4.89 on revenue of ~$60.67B, representing a ~150% YoY EPS increase from the year-ago $1.85. Brent above $100 throughout Q3 supports results.

Goldman est XOM EPS ~$4.10 vs $3.87 consensus

headline: Oil prices on track for 4th monthly gain in October; WTI +14% as US-Iran conflict persists
summary: Crude oil prices were on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain in October 2026, with WTI up approximately 14% month-to-date as the US-Iran conflict continued to disrupt Strait of Hormuz shipping. Brent was also significantly higher on the month. The sustained rally has added to inflationary pressures and complicated the Fed's decision-making.
key_facts: Elevated oil adding to US inflation (PCE 3.6%)

headline: North Korea linked to Binance $6.3B hack by Chainalysis and TRM Labs; $2.54B frozen
summary: Blockchain analytics firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs attributed the $6.3B Binance hack to North Korea, citing transaction patterns consistent with prior North Korean crypto heists including the Bybit attack. About $2.54-3B has been frozen on-chain. The attack was traced to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop enabling unauthorized withdrawal transactions. Binance said no wallet private keys were exposed.
key_facts: Chainalysis and TRM Labs: North Korea responsible
Compromised DevOps engineer laptop entry point

headline: ECB's Lagarde announces February 2027 departure alongside rate hold decision
summary: ECB President Christine Lagarde announced she would depart in February 2027 at the same press conference where the ECB held rates steady at 2.50%. The announcement adds uncertainty to the ECB's policy path into 2027, as the central bank grapples with elevated inflation (3.8%) and potential energy-driven price pressures from the Middle East conflict.
key_facts: Energy prices driving upside inflation risk

headline: Microsoft Azure revenue +48% in Q1 FY27; commercial RPO surges 73% to $677B backlog
summary: Microsoft's Azure cloud division posted 48% revenue growth in Q1 FY2027, contributing to total Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9B (+30%). The commercial remaining performance obligation—a measure of contracted future revenue—surged 73% to $677B, signaling strong enterprise AI and cloud demand. Microsoft's agents-and-infrastructure segment generated $76.8B in revenue, up 25%.

headline: Warsh: Fed held pre-election; politics played 'no role'; Dec hike now 73-85% priced
summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh emphasized that politics played 'no role' in the decision to hold rates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, and that the FOMC is waiting for an 'accumulation of more information' before further action. With two hawkish dissents (Cook and Hammack) and hot PCE data, markets moved to price a 73-85% probability for a December rate hike.
key_facts: Warsh: politics played 'no role' in hold decision
Fed plans fewer annual meetings starting 2027

The company confirmed its special committee has been formed but no terms have been agreed. The stock gain adds to earlier excitement following SpaceX's Q3 earnings beat and first-ever quarterly profit.
key_facts: TSLA above $400 for first time since Jul 10
Driven by SpaceX merger committee formation
SpaceX Q3 revenue $14.6B, first quarterly profit

summary: Intel guided Q4 2026 revenue of $15.0-16.0B and non-GAAP EPS of $0.25, disappointing analysts who expected stronger sequential growth following the Q3 results.
